note: Reconstructed 2026-09-10 from the saved results (reconstruct.ts) plus selectors read out of the mirror snapshot and our own page, not guessed. The reference root is div.flex.relative, the wrapper holding both buttons: data-geist-menu-button marks the TRIGGER and there are 15 of those, one per root, so it cannot be the marker. `previews` names 0..3 on the reference: the mirror carries six preview boxes and our docs page has four, and the last two reference previews have no counterpart. Verified by counting: both sides give 6+2+1+6 = 15 roots over those four, matching the saved run. `states` is [""] INSIDE each side, not at the top level: the census defaults to four passes (base, data-hover, data-focus, data-active) and reads a top-level key not at all, so a misplaced one silently measures three states the saved run never did. Base alone matches the saved run — the reference's hover and focus land on data-hover/data-focus that react-aria sets, which the census cannot drive. `textParts` is main and mainLabel, whose width follows the button's own text. Both labels are acme-button's own `label` part, reached with a >> hop through the button's shadow root. `main` and `trigger` also hop: the reference's <button> is the real control, and on ours acme-button is only the HOST — reading the host gives cursor:auto, position:static and font-weight:400 for a button that is none of those. The trigger's glyph is NOT reached that way: it sits in the light DOM inside .inner, so its selector is a plain descendant one; the trigger's is the box the reference centres with flex, which is why triggerLabel and mainLabel read differently.
